facts.text: Grand Saline takes its name from the vast salt deposits southeast of the town, most of which are owned by Morton Salt.
A parcel of land was donated to the railroad, prompting the construction of a depot that gave the stop the name Grand Saline.
The City of Grand Saline was incorporated in 1895, replacing the earlier community of Jordan's Saline as residents moved north to the new city.
Early actress Louise Fazenda, wife of Warner Brothers' Hal Wallis, once lived in the Lone Star Hotel in Grand Saline.
Grand Saline proudly displays mementos from hometown favorite Chris Tomlin, the award‑winning Christian singer‑songwriter.
Ancient Caddo and Cherokee tribes discovered a salt prairie south of Grand Saline, using evaporated salt from the brine stream as a trade commodity.
